title: Genus is nondecreasing under a nonconstant cover of smooth curves
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field and let $C,D$ be smooth proper geometrically integral curves (integral finite-type schemes of dimension one) over $\Omega$. For every nonconstant $\Omega$-morphism $u:C\to D$, one has $g(C)\geq g(D)$. Here $g(C)=\dim_\Omega H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$ and similarly for $D$, as in [def-sc-genus]. Nonconstant means that $u$ does not factor through an $\Omega$-rational point of $D$. The assertion includes inseparable morphisms and fields of positive characteristic; no separability of $k(C)/k(D)$ is assumed.

The notions used are [def-weil-field], [def-weil-algebraic-closure], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-pure-dimension], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-pc-genus], [def-pc-field-extension]. Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. A finite separable extension is a finite-dimensional field extension whose elements have separable minimal polynomials. Group actions on schemes and fields may be nonfaithful and semilinear on the ground field.

proof.text: Geometric integrality over the field gives integrality of C and D, hence irreducibility. Their unique irreducible components are the whole spaces, so pure dimension one implies topologicalKrullDim C = topologicalKrullDim D = 1. Properness and smoothness supply the finite-type separated curve structures. For an irreducible smooth scheme over a field, dimension one gives smoothness of relative dimension one. Apply [lem-pc-genus-agrees-sc] to rewrite both arithmetic genera as Hom.genus. If the target genus is zero the inequality follows from nonnegativity; otherwise it is at least one and 2g(D)-2 is nonnegative.

source.place: Definition of genus; the genus-zero case and the reduction to positive target genus.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-curve-frobenius-separable-factorization] to $u:C\to D$. Its hypotheses are exactly the smoothness, properness, geometric integrality, dimension one, algebraic closedness, and nonconstancy assumed here. We obtain $u=v\circ F$ with $C'$ again a smooth proper geometrically integral curve and $v:C'\to D$ nonconstant with finite separable function-field extension. In characteristic zero $C'=C$ and $F$ is the identity; in characteristic $p>0$, $C'=C^{(p^n)}$ is the specified base change of $C$ along $\varphi_n:a\mapsto a^{p^n}$.

source.place: Tag 0CD2 (curves-proposition-unwind-morphism-smooth), with its characteristic-zero identity case.

proof.text: In characteristic zero the equality and heterogeneous equality of structure maps supplied by step 2 identify the genus of C-prime with that of C. In positive characteristic p, substitute the equality of C-prime with the pullback along the specified iterateFrobeniusOfPrime endomorphism and the equality of its structure map with the second projection. Install precisely the algebra structure induced by that endomorphism [def-pc-field-extension]. Smoothness of relative dimension one is preserved under this pullback. Rewrite both Hom.genus values as arithmeticGenus by [lem-pc-genus-agrees-sc], then apply Scheme.arithmeticGenus_pullback, the structure-sheaf degree-one consequence of [lem-sc-flat-base-change-coherent], also recorded in [lem-pc-genus-base-change]. This gives g(C-prime)=g(C) without identifying the Frobenius endomorphism with the identity.

source.place: Tag 0CD0 (curves-lemma-purely-inseparable-smooth-genus), proof using Tag 0BY9 (curves-lemma-genus-base-change); existing flat coherent base change supplies the explicit H^1 dimension equality.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-curve-riemann-hurwitz-numerical] to $v:C'\to D$. Step 2 supplies every geometric hypothesis and the finite separable function-field extension. Thus, for the positive integer $d=[k(C'):k(D)]$, there is an integer $r\geq0$ with $2g(C')-2=d(2g(D)-2)+r$. The lemma uses the effective different, so this application includes wildly ramified separable maps in positive characteristic.

Since $d\geq1$ and $2g(D)-2\geq0$, we have $d(2g(D)-2)\geq2g(D)-2$. Adding $r\geq0$ to this and using step 4 gives $2g(C')-2\geq2g(D)-2$, hence $g(C')\geq g(D)$ by adding $2$ and dividing by the positive integer $2$. Substitute $g(C')=g(C)$ from step 3 to obtain $g(C)\geq g(D)$. Together with the case $g(D)=0$ in step 1 this proves the assertion.

reviewed_lean.note: Every clause matches the node. Omega is an algebraically closed field of any characteristic. C and D are Scheme.{u} over Spec Omega with Smooth, IsProper and GeometricallyIntegral on the structure maps and IsPureDimension 1; finite type follows from IsProper. The map is an Omega-morphism (hf), and hnonconstant excludes exactly factoring through an Omega-rational section, as the node defines it. The conclusion arithmeticGenus Omega D <= arithmeticGenus Omega C is dim H^1(O) (def-pc-genus record, EulerChar.lean:79), the node's genus. The def-sc-genus Lean record Hom.genus is the Omega^1 form and agrees only through sorry'd Serre duality, so using arithmeticGenus is correct and adds no second definition. No separability, finiteness or char hypothesis. Edge cases genus 0, char p, Frobenius, isomorphisms and empty scheme checked; single universe u. lean.statement is verbatim in the file. The node equals the live node except for lean, and no live module exists. Docstrings carry Stacks 0C1B/0CD2/0CD0 (curves.tex labels at l.2207/2624/2671), the blueprint id and the five proof steps; the proof is sorry only. Not recompiled (no change).
